chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

"When a man escorts his brother, he should shorten [his prayer]." I asked, "Which is better: that he fasts or that he escorts him and breaks his fast?" He said, "He should escort him, because God has exempted him [from the full prayer] when he escorts him."

key_terms.شَيَّعَ: to escort or accompany (specifically to the graveyard or mosque)
key_terms.وَضَعَهُ: He has exempted it / removed the obligation
key_terms.يُقَصِّرْ: he should shorten (referring to the shortening of the four-rak'ah prayer to two)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler who escorts someone else regarding shortening prayer and fasting?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the virtue of *tashyi'* (escorting a companion), establishing it as a superior act of worship to fasting for a traveler due to its role as a valid excuse for shortening prayers (*qasr*). The Imam clarifies that the physical act of escorting carries sufficient spiritual weight to justify the concession of *qasr*, emphasizing the social dimension of travel in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the balance between individual devotion and communal solidarity during journeys.
